hypotheses.statement: Test a minimal port of DeepGEMM #452’s contiguous SM90 FP8 MQA epilogue into the pinned H200 build, conditional on proving active header use and a safe numerical domain. The supplied installed excerpt retains fmaxf and unhalved KV scales, establishing a source-level delta but no execution or bottleneck evidence. The PR author reports H200 microbenchmark gains from substituting full-rate FADD with an absolute-value operand and compensating both output scales. Our transfer hypothesis is lower exposed prefill time and TTFT where uncached requests invoke this kernel; warm-prefix and paged-only traffic should benefit little directly. Compare against the equally compiled, warmed stock epilogue at unchanged launch settings. Reject unconditional bit-exactness: overflow, underflow, exceptional values and downstream top-k stability must be resolved before serving tests. Serving value remains unmeasured.
hypotheses.observed_bottleneck: None measured. Observed supplied source text retains the original transform and both uncompensated scale multiplications. The runtime snapshot configures prefix caching and chunked prefill but does not establish kernel dispatch. Author-reported results: H200, 132 SMs, SM90A; +4.8% kernel throughput for SQ=2048, SKV=8192, H=64, BF16, CP=1, and average +3.7% across 192 contiguous cases. The selected-shape measurements use best of three repetitions. These are neither independently reproduced observations nor serving gains; timing distributions, worst-case regressions, CP meaning and D for the 8K case are unknown.
hypotheses.mechanism: Source proposal: replace fmaxf(x,0) with x+fabsf(x), then multiply each existing KV scale by 0.5. The author attributes improvement to replacing half-rate FMNMX with full-rate FADD using an absolute-value operand modifier. Transfer inference: this can shorten an exposed contiguous-prefill epilogue without changing scoring coverage or launch geometry. Instruction issue-rate improvement does not establish kernel or serving speedup. The separate paged kernel receives no direct optimization.
hypotheses.proposed_change: First inspect the pinned process’s import/include resolution, DeepGEMM revision, JIT cache provenance and contiguous-prefill call sites. The visible header lacks the change, but the executing implementation remains unknown. If eligible and absent, port only commit ee53a16b089d441cbfc4020cd558c1f05f623d97’s transform replacement and two half-scale folds into an isolated build, with a comment coupling the changes. Retain the stock build for rollback. Rebuild and identify affected JIT specializations; require numerical qualification before serving evaluation. If the supported input/scaling domain cannot justify the transformation, retain stock behavior rather than enabling it unconditionally.
hypotheses.code_surface: vllm/third_party/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm90_fp8_mqa_logits.cuh: transform lambda and v_0/v_1 scale multiplications. Also inspect, without assuming their contents, the active JIT loader, contiguous-MQA dispatch and downstream top-k consumer. No paged-scoring, selector, launch-geometry or scheduler changes belong in this arm.
hypotheses.applicability: Plausible upstream port for H200 SM90, supported by a matching installed source excerpt and author-reported H200 tests. Deployment qualification remains deferred pending active-header, invocation, shape and numerical checks. Record actual SQ, SKV, H, D, output dtype, masking, scale layout and execution mode; MBT16384 and an 8K prompt do not determine kernel shapes. Preserve the supplied vLLM and serving commits, model revision, two TP1/DP4/EP4 replicas, API2, seq64 and all other baseline settings.
hypotheses.predicted_direction: Conditionally lower contiguous-kernel duration and cold-prefill TTFT; possible throughput and parameterized cost improvements when this work limits service capacity. Direct paged-decode TPOT benefit is not predicted. Mixed-load TPOT may improve indirectly through reduced prefill interference. Warm-prefix benefit should diminish with removed eligible work. Effect sizes are unknown; zero benefit and regressions remain possible.

alternatives.explanation: Stores, reductions, memory traffic or another stage dominate; faster ReLU issue has little exposed value. The closed #303 discusses broader kernel changes and includes an anecdotal long-context slowdown, without establishing its cause.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Use a separate mechanism diagnostic on actual invocation shapes to measure epilogue instructions, kernel duration and critical-path exposure. An instruction substitution without reduced exposed time rejects the proposed bottleneck explanation for that workload.

alternatives.explanation: Apparent improvement comes from unequal JIT warming, prefix residency, routing or run drift.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compile and warm both variants equally, independently control KV-cache state, verify final-rank placement and cached-token counts, and alternate matched full-run A/B blocks. Include confirmed warm-prefix and paged-only negative controls.

alternatives.explanation: The changed arithmetic alters logits or top-k selections, producing a workload or quality change that masquerades as faster equivalent execution.
alternatives.distinguishing_test: Compare identical-input logits, masks and top-k sets before serving tests; then compare quality, exact output-token counts and all-rank draft/verify/accepted counters. Repeatability within one variant does not establish baseline equivalence.

evidence.quote: Paged MQA logits (separate kernel, untouched) is unaffected.
I am seeing a similar slowdown with fp8_mqa_logits on long-context prefill

novelty.scientific: No novelty claimed; this is an existing arithmetic and instruction-selection technique.
novelty.implementation: A narrow deployment port of an existing SM90 patch, with explicit numerical and JIT-provenance qualification.
novelty.workload: Evaluate exposure under native H200 seq64 agent-f75 and Mooncake traffic, using cold/warm discrimination to separate prefill savings from cache effects.
novelty.nearest_prior_art: DeepGEMM #452 directly supplies the proposed optimization and attributes an analogous packed implementation to SM100. #303 concerns broader stores, staging and occupancy changes; its closure rationale is unknown.
novelty.specific_delta: Replace the installed contiguous epilogue’s fmaxf transform and compensate both KV scales, while retaining the baseline’s launch settings and surrounding serving behavior.

experiment.control: The attested baseline with its stock fmaxf contiguous epilogue, independently rebuilt using the same toolchain and launch configurations and equally JIT-warmed. This is the strongest evidenced static comparator; the packet establishes no equivalent flag or stronger drop-in implementation. Keep precision, scheduling, topology, speculation, telemetry and cache preparation identical.
experiment.treatment: Future experiment only: follow attestation, activation, correctness, unprofiled screening, separate mechanism diagnosis, then paired confirmation and held-out evaluation. Change only the coupled three-line epilogue operation. Inspect generated SM90A code for the relevant FMNMX-to-FADD substitution, compensation and unexpected spills or instruction growth. Across every replica/rank, count patched-kernel hits over independently identified eligible contiguous-prefill call opportunities, reporting shapes and score volume; also report eligible calls over all prefill calls. Join requests to final ranks. Use equally warmed JIT artifacts with separately controlled cold KV prefixes and confirmed warm-prefix hits.
experiment.metrics: Primary: native agent-f75 8K/1K prefix workload and fixed-schedule Mooncake anchors adapted to seq64. Record TTFT distributions/tails, request TPOT=(last-first token time)/(server output tokens-1), exact tokens, throughput, qualified request goodput and replay lag. Record cached/uncached prompt tokens, KV blocks, preemption and all-rank draft/verify/accepted counter deltas, resets and missing coverage. Separately measure shape-specific kernel duration and exposed prefill time; exclude profiled runs from the serving frontier. Confirm small gains with at least five alternating paired full-run blocks, baseline-drift checks and paired uncertainty intervals; requests are not independent experimental units.
experiment.supports_if: Active-artifact and numerical gates pass; eligible calls show the intended instruction change and reduced exposed prefill time; paired unprofiled primary runs show an improvement exceeding a predeclared practical threshold with uncertainty excluding no improvement, while quality and tail/TPOT guardrails pass. The effect follows eligible uncached work and weakens where verified cache hits remove it. A benefit confined to long-context diagnostics supports only that narrower applicability.
experiment.rejects_if: Adequate primary-workload coverage establishes that the changed kernel is unused or already equivalent; a supported-domain correctness failure has no acceptable remedy; or sufficiently precise paired results exclude the predeclared useful gain or show unacceptable quality, TTFT-tail, TPOT or goodput regressions. A microbenchmark win without primary serving value rejects promotion for this baseline.
experiment.inconclusive_if: Active include/JIT provenance, numerical domain or dispatch cannot be established; zero hits lack adequate opportunity coverage; telemetry is missing; cache state or arrivals are unmatched; drift or intervals cannot resolve the useful-effect threshold; or only source-author microbenchmarks and profiled measurements are available. Unknown gates remain deferred, not qualified.
experiment.held_out_condition: Reserve distinct long-context lengths, ragged chunk boundaries, mixed prefill/decode arrivals and cold/warm prefix conditions without tuning on them. Keep the cache-isolated 1K/1K diagnostic separate from native anchors. Include paged-only execution as a negative control and verify actual residual contiguous work in warm-cache cases. Seq128 remains a separate configuration arm.
experiment.correctness: Compare stock and treatment against an appropriate higher-precision reference, preserving masks, scale semantics and output dtype. Establish bounds for accumulators, weighted products, reductions and scale halving, including rounding and flush-to-zero behavior. Analytical objection, not an observed failure: finite positive FLT_MAX overflows when doubled; with unit weight and original scale 0.5, the original scalar contribution is finite while delayed compensation cannot recover it. Test extreme finite values, subnormal scales, signed zero, NaN and infinities, plus real-input distributions. Require downstream top-k-set agreement and ordering under the deployed tie policy, including near ties. Author-reported self-consistency is insufficient. Exercise applicable graph/eager, chunking, cache-hit/miss and distributed paths; run a quality subset because arithmetic changes. Map relevant G01–G05 once their definitions are available. Speculative acceptance is diagnostic, not a correctness score.
experiment.cost: Cheap first step: source/configuration/JIT-provenance inspection, followed only if warranted by a small isolated header port. Compilation, correctness and later GPU experiment costs are unknown; none were incurred here. With full eight-GPU node price P8 per hour, report cost per qualified output token as P8 × elapsed_seconds / (3600 × qualified_output_tokens). Keep P8 unset; do not transfer B200 pricing.

hypotheses.revision_reason: Initial hypothesis narrowed to a conditional contiguous-prefill port after addressing the supplied numerical objections. Universal bit-exactness and paged-decode benefit are excluded from the claim. No earlier hypothesis is revised.

gaps: Only supplied sources were analyzed; no tools, file modifications, retrieval, integration or GPU execution occurred. The requested thirteen-repository research coverage is not established.

The visible installed epilogue establishes a source delta, but active JIT include resolution, artifact provenance, compiler settings, invocation frequency, actual shapes and critical-path exposure remain unknown.
The author’s H200 microbenchmarks are unreproduced. Raw distributions, uncertainty, worst-case regressions, complete input ranges and target serving effect sizes are unknown.
Numerical safety, top-k equivalence and quality preservation are unresolved. The supplied excerpts do not establish a sufficient scaling/range invariant.

#452 merge status and exhaustive review coverage are unknown. #303’s closure rationale, complaint hardware, exact workload and slowdown magnitude are unknown; its closure does not demonstrate rejection of #452’s mechanism.
G01–G05 definitions, production H200 SLOs, practical-effect thresholds and node pricing are unavailable. Required applicability and correctness gates remain deferred pending inspection and testing.
